name: Danish Power Limited
sector: Renewable-duty and power transformers; control panels
summary: Danish has demonstrated transformer growth and a credible order-driven runway, but recent capital returns and cash conversion lag headline earnings. The new ₹150–200 crore expansion is explicitly funded in the scenarios. At ₹975.90, the conditional base return is below the 15 percent hurdle; this is a valuation-sensitive watchlist business, not a high-conviction compounder.
identity_note: Issuer annual and NSE filings verify NSE SME listing on 29 October 2024; September capital reconciliation and October actual SM trading cross-check current identity and capital.
score_note: All canonical factors supported with explicit assumptions and full coverage. No critical gate or persistent CAP/CASH cap applied. The low modeled return affects R directly, not a fabricated quality failure.

sections.title: Research Header and Scope
sections.text: Danish Power Limited, NSE SME DANISH, ISIN INE0YU901016; listed 29 October 2024. Cutoff 20 October 2026. Official 19 October close ₹975.90; 19,691,610 issued shares and 150-share lot. Consolidated March 2026 Ind AS accounts anchor the model; older GAAP/scope distinctions are labeled. The analytical hurdle is 15 percent nominal, before investor tax, and the reference position is ₹5 lakh. FY2027–FY2031 annual forecasts use a five-year comparison return; the approximately 4.45-year entry-to-March-2031 return is shown separately. G1–G4 are conditional. [S1][S5][S6][S12]

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: This is an operating manufacturer with demonstrated production and revenue expansion, not merely a renewable-energy narrative. However, growth consumed cash, recent incremental capital returns are weak and the September project creates another large reinvestment cycle. Base return of about 7.6 percent is below the 15 percent hurdle despite growth. Watch for cash-funded utilization and a more forgiving price; neither an order headline nor low opening debt alone makes the stock attractive. [S1][S9][S10]

sections.title: Scorecard and Gates
sections.text: BQS 5.98, Growth Quality GQS 6.35, and conditional IAS 3.995. GOV 6, MOAT 6, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 4, CASH 4, BAL 7, EXEC 6 and EARN 5. IAS reuses BQS exactly, with R 2, D 3, P 4 and L 8. Coverage is 100 percent with no override. Medium confidence reflects specific assumptions about ramp, deposits, collections and financing, not an audited forecast. Position-specific execution may change IAS.

sections.title: Business Model
sections.text: Inverter-duty transformers for renewable projects, power/distribution transformers and control/relay panels drive the business. FY2026 transformer sales were ₹478.64 crore and panels ₹35.87 crore within ₹521.45 crore consolidated revenue. Property-holding Evernest and the new sheet-metal subsidiary do not create a material acquired manufacturing-revenue jump. The operating model is equipment supply, not electricity/CER generation; an inconsistent segment note must not be used to redefine it. Upfront-paid leasehold land is not unpaid lease debt. [S1][S8]

sections.title: Competitive Position and Moat
sections.text: Customer qualification, engineering/testing and manufacturing reliability are genuine entry frictions. Production increased from 4,498 to 5,468 MVA, corroborating product demand. But historical top-ten customers represented 88.04 percent of FY2024 sales, with purchase-order rather than long-term contractual relationships; current concentration was not equivalently disclosed. Top-ten suppliers represented 38.70 percent of FY2024 purchases, and volatile copper, steel and oil costs matter. These facts support a useful operating franchise, not monopoly pricing or a verified peer-relative excess-return moat. [S1][S8]

sections.title: Demonstrated Revenue Growth
sections.text: Revenue FY2021–FY2026 was ₹117.7804/148.6336/188.7006/332.4767/426.7098/521.4466 crore. The preselected five-year CAGR is about 34.66 percent, versus roughly 40.3 percent for three years. Latest growth slowed to 22.20 percent after 28.34 percent, while transformer MVA grew 21.57 percent and transformer sales about 22.0 percent. REV starts at 9 and is adjusted down one for sustained full-year deceleration, not a single quarter. Exact price/mix is unavailable; the volume cross-check and property-subsidiary scope make ordinary reported growth usable. [S1][S2][S8]

sections.title: Runway and Reinvestment Economics
sections.text: Existing capacity reached 11,000 MVA. September management reported an order book above ₹600 crore and FY2027 sales guidance above ₹700 crore; the model uses ₹650 crore, not uncritically relabeled guidance. A further 12,000–15,000 MVA project, up to 400 kV, was announced at ₹150–200 crore over 18–24 months, funded from accruals/debt. The sheet-metal project target moved from July to November 2026. Higher-voltage trials and approvals remain gates to revenue. Recent BESS/export awards support opportunity but are not added again to modeled sales. Adjusted funded capital rose from ₹197.67 crore to ₹296.01 crore; incremental core NOPAT return about 5.65 percent is below an assumed 12–15 percent capital cost. Ramp timing is a possible explanation, not proof of eventual excess return. [S1][S3][S9][S10][S11]

sections.title: Governance and Capital Allocation
sections.text: Dinesh and Shivam held 64.96 and 8.59 percent at March 2026. Family director remuneration of ₹7.286 crore was about 10.6 percent of group PAT; related Tashe purchases were ₹7.66 crore. Monitor pricing and approvals without assuming abuse. The audit opinion was unmodified, while IFC documentation was inadequate and material observations were reported rectified. The ₹6.31 lakh transition difference is only about 0.116 percent of comparative PAT; copied segment wording, a small deferred-tax note mismatch and omitted comparative columns indicate disclosure controls needing improvement, not unusable core accounts. August board disclosure records a paid fine for a one-day RPT submission delay. ESOP authorization covers up to 500,000 options, with exercise price floor ₹10; authorization is not a grant. September capital reconciliation confirms no issued-share change. [S1][S12][S14][S16]

sections.title: Financial Quality and Cash Conversion
sections.text: FY2026 PAT ₹68.9818 crore converted into CFO ₹42.5018 crore, 61.6 percent; two comparable years converted only 22.7 percent. Cash capex ₹74.146 crore left pre-financing FCF −₹31.6442 crore. Older positive cash flows prevent a persistent-negative classification. Core EBITDA excluding other income was ₹92.4368 crore, not the roughly 19 percent margin that includes non-operating income; core EBIT grew only about 9.5 percent versus PAT growth of 26.3 percent. Lower finance costs and a ₹1.253 crore prior-tax credit helped. The cash-flow closing ₹91.8336 crore includes ₹24.0676 crore cash plus ₹67.766 crore deposits: this is a reconciled classification, not missing cash. FD restrictions and government balances remain distinct from spendable cash. [S1][S2][S8]

sections.title: Historical and Forensic Review
sections.text: The IPO prospectus disclosed an August 2023 MCA show-cause notice concerning delayed cost-audit filing for FY2020 and the company’s September reply seeking closure. It also listed a revenue-department application concerning a ₹1,71,480 PF disallowance and six historical TDS defaults totaling ₹52.82 lakh. These were disclosed procedural/tax matters at the prospectus date, not findings of fraud; current closure status is unverified. No recovery from company-filed utility-interest claims is included in valuation. FY2025 original-GAAP CFO and the later Ind AS comparative differ through the disclosed transition; the series are not silently spliced. Revaluation OCI ₹34.3684 crore is noncash and excluded from core earnings. Goodwill ₹12.5677 crore and the Evernest intercompany/CCD adjustment are retained in the capital analysis; group PAT is used, not higher parent PAT. March monitoring reports all IPO proceeds used within objects, with earlier deployment delays and management explanations, not diversion. The CSR shortfall ₹0.3054 crore and April restricted-bank transfer are treated conservatively with a zero-additional-cost overlap test. Contingent bank guarantees ₹107.50 crore are not all booked as debt but are stress-tested. [S1][S8][S15]

sections.title: Valuation and Funding Scenarios
sections.text: At ₹975.90, equity value is ₹1,921.70 crore, trailing group P/E 27.86 and cash-only EV/core EBITDA about 20.55. Debt ₹2.1707 crore, cash ₹24.0676 crore and deposits ₹67.766 crore are separately reconciled. Full annual scenarios include actual operating WC ₹138.6603 crore, gross opening tax ₹22 crore, conditional government-asset recovery, retained/settled legacy benefits, current claims already in WC, new project capex, average-debt interest, collateral reserves and prior-holder dividends. Bear/base/bull terminal prices are approximately ₹397.23/₹1,408.32/₹2,922.90; five-year comparison returns −16.45/7.61/24.53 percent. Peak year-end debt is ₹213.87/₹68.38/₹4.24 crore, not a lender commitment. Severe combined stress exhausts equity. At 12/15/18 percent hurdles, base-dependent entry prices are roughly ₹799/₹700/₹616, not observable fair values. Margin/WC/multiple, capex, deposits, recoveries, benefit timing, dilution and transaction-cost sensitivities are supplied. [S1][S5][S9][S10][S12][S17]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold appreciation over five years require 37.97 and 58.49 percent annual returns. Linked reverse cases solve the required revenue growth, capital, debt and terminal value rather than simply raising P/E. Even before qualification/execution risk, they demand far more than the base operating path; additional capacity above ₹2,000 crore sales receives an explicit capital charge. That scaling rule is an illustrative engineering proxy, not evidence that extreme volumes can be delivered. The 5× and 10× cases require roughly 55.46 and 80.15 percent constant revenue growth, with peak year-end debt around ₹858.36 and ₹2,652.24 crore. The bull case is about threefold, not fivefold. Classification: possible only under substantially stronger economics and repeated funded scaling, not a demonstrated or probable multibagger. [S1][S9][S10]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Verify sheet-metal commissioning against November 2026, higher-voltage type tests/approvals, order conversion versus ₹700 crore guidance, and MVA rather than orders alone. Track receivable aging, government/GST recovery, restricted deposit schedules, funded project spending and cash tax. Compare incremental operating returns after ramp with capital cost; a profit increase caused mainly by interest/tax normalization is insufficient. Monitor promoter/RPT remuneration, ESOP grants/exercise, updated encumbrances and actual debt sanctions. Refresh executable quote/depth before implementation. [S1][S9][S10][S12]

sections.title: Bear Case and What Would Change the View
sections.text: The bear mechanism combines weak utilization, lower margins, slow collections and an unfinished expensive project, creating refinancing and potential dilution. A guarantee call worsens the cash burden but is not presumed. Counterevidence would be cash-backed utilization growth, disciplined project spend, confirmed free deposits and repeat higher-voltage customer approvals with attractive returns. A lower price alone improves expected return but does not cure poor capital allocation. Minor note discrepancies alone would not overturn the investment case; persistent unreconciled cash or material related-party extraction would.

sections.title: Source Coverage and Limitations
sections.text: Primary review covers the FY2026 annual statements/audit/notes, FY2025 annual, IPO financial/business/legal history, May investor call, September expansion and AGM, proceeds monitoring, later order awards and October capital/governance filings. Official market data cover all 60 sessions and current lot; decoded REG1 carries a generic SME irregular-trading caution despite observed daily trading, and named-list absence is not blanket clearance. The historical rating URL could not be independently reopened; issuer references are not substituted for a fresh rating rationale. No verified FY2027 interim balance sheet or live order-book depth is available. These limitations remain explicit rather than presented as audited forecasts.

GOV.reason: Concentrated family control, meaningful remuneration/RPT and documentation defects constrain score; small corrections and paid late-filing fine do not establish material minority abuse.

MOAT.reason: Qualification, design/testing and real production scale are advantages; project purchasing and historical customer concentration prevent a durable pricing-power claim.

REV.reason: Five-year CAGR about 34.66 percent starts at REV9. One-point downward adjustment reflects two successive slower full years (28.34 and 22.20 percent), supported by volume, not a single-quarter signal.

DUR.reason: Renewables, BESS and export orders offer a credible multi-year runway, constrained by qualification and customer/project concentration.

CAP.reason: Recent incremental core NOPAT return around 5.65 percent is below assumed capital cost; staged capacity explains timing but does not yet prove an attractive return.

CASH.reason: Current 61.6 percent conversion and only 22.7 percent across two comparable years, plus negative post-capex cash, limit quality. Earlier positive CFO prevents a persistent-negative override.

BAL.reason: Low drawn opening debt and cash cushion support resilience, but deposits are partly collateral and 150–200 crore expansion plus WC require funding.

EXEC.reason: Existing 11000 MVA capacity and volume growth demonstrate execution; delayed sheet-metal start and new voltage qualification prevent a higher score.

EARN.reason: PAT grew faster than core EBIT because lower finance cost and a prior-tax credit helped. Core growth is real but headline profit overstates operating acceleration.

R.reason: Supported conditional base five-year comparison IRR 7.61 percent minus 15 percent hurdle gives −7.39 percentage points, in the −10 to below −7 band. Actual shorter fiscal horizon is separately disclosed.

D.reason: Bear value is about 59.3 percent below entry with 213.87 crore peak debt; joint severe stress exhausts equity. Base funding remains manageable but bear financing is not committed.

P.reason: Base operating expansion still misses the hurdle after multiple normalization. About 27 percent constant growth is needed for a 15 percent return; collection, margin and execution errors matter.

L.reason: Starting band9 from sub-two-day capacity is downgraded one for 29.28 percent position-size lot and unverified spread/depth. Complete observed trading history supports a conditional score, not guaranteed execution.

limitations: Close/last is historical, not executable bid. No bid-ask spread or depth. Absent sessions must not be interpreted as no trade unless listed throughout and not missing data. Recent IPO prelisting dates are not zero trading days; use shortened sample. Series changes/multiple rows/corporate actions require issuer review. valuation.status: Conditional linked annual operating, funding and terminal-equity scenarios
valuation.units: INR crore except shares and INR per share
valuation.opening_WC_formula: 91.3873 inventory + 111.1562 receivables + 4.2021 current financial assets - 0.0002 foundation advance + 0.9051 operating security/EMD + 1.0900 prepayments + 3.2008 supplier advances - 40.6074 trade payables - 11.3401 other financial current liabilities - 19.7158 other current liabilities - 1.6177 current non-tax provisions = 138.6603.
methodology: Consolidated March 2026 actual opening balances are used, not forecast ratios applied backward. Annual dates FY2027–FY2031 span the remaining FY2027 and subsequent years; October entry returns use a conventional five-year horizon to FY2031 terminal, approximately six months longer than the remaining March calendar period. These are not five complete post-entry reported periods. A four-and-a-half-year return sensitivity is supplied separately.

Existing upfront-paid leasehold land and IPO proceeds are not financed or bought again. Gross current tax 22 is paid once in FY2027; current statutory, employee, expense and non-tax provision claims are already in operating WC. Government balances 27.3372 are not assumed verified tax offsets: half is conditionally recovered in FY2028 in base; zero/full and alternative dates are tested. Unrecovered balances receive no terminal value.

Noncurrent employee benefits 2.3065, warranty 0.1598 and decommissioning 0.0571 total 2.5234. Core scenarios retain and deduct this opening obligation from terminal equity; FY2027/FY2029 settlements remove it after one cash payment. Recurring employee and warranty costs are in forecast operating margins. Deferred tax 15.0986, largely associated with revaluation, is not assumed immediately payable; no land sale or separate land terminal value is modeled. Forecast cash tax 26 percent is a simplified assumption, not a complete deferred-tax schedule.

Unspent CSR 0.3054 is separately reserved and spent once in FY2027 as a conservative incremental cost. Its mapping within reported general payables is not separately identifiable, so a zero-additional-cash case quantifies possible overlap rather than mechanically claiming another liability. Recurring future CSR is included in operating margins. This small mapping uncertainty is not a critical reliability hold.

All opening deposits are initially reserved, not assumed spendable. Forecast collateral requirement is 5 percent of sales in base; only incremental shortfall is deposited, and only terminal excess is credited to equity. Operating collateral remains with the business and is not added again. Initial release 40 and 3/8 percent collateral cases are assumptions, not verified bank restrictions. Deposit interest uses average balances at 5.5 percent and is taxed separately from operating EBITDA.

The September 2026 additional 12000–15000 MVA project costs 150–200 crore by management estimate over 18–24 months. Base 175 is phased 25/50/25 percent across FY2027–FY2029, plus existing net capital commitments 10.4366 and ordinary maintenance/growth capex 2 percent of sales. Paid CWIP 15.0181 and advances 7.716 are not purchased again. Beyond 2000 crore annual sales, extra capacity capex of 0.16 per rupee additional sales is charged before allowing growth; this is an illustrative scaling proxy, not verified engineering capacity. Higher 20/25 completion cases are illustrative stress sizes, not verified bounds. Existing depreciation 7.4186 continues, new capex depreciates 10 percent annually with half-year first-year convention; no goodwill depreciation or repeated land purchase.

Base FY2027 revenue 650 is below management guidance above 700 and implies about 24.65 percent growth, modestly above FY2026 volume growth, conditional on the expanded existing plant and disclosed order book, followed by 18/18/16/14 percent growth. Production, qualification and utilization must support it. Announced orders are not added a second time to these sales. Core margins exclude extrapolation of interest income and revaluation; 13/17/19 percent are scenario assumptions, not audited segment forecasts.

Funding uses average opening/closing debt, including half-year new draw interest solved with tax/cash circularity at 11 percent base. Minimum cash is 5 crore. Required borrowing is not sanctioned financing. No rescue issue is assumed. Current 19,691,610 shares are retained; authorized but unverified grants of up to 500,000 ESOPs are paired with exercise cash only in explicit terminal exercise sensitivities.

FY2026 dividend 2 rupees per share is 3.938322 crore and leaves issuer cash once in FY2027. It belonged to the September record-date owners and is not a dividend return to an October buyer. No later dividend is forecast; surplus stays in terminal cash.

Impairment is a noncash PAT loss, added back to CFO; replacement investment enters delta WC against impaired opening assets once. Guarantee-call stress is an incremental cash expense with no assumed recovery or tax shield. A guarantee face value is not automatically debt. Terminal multiples apply to core EBITDA and no operating WC/PPE/land is added again.

gates.reason: Family control and related remuneration/procurement require ongoing safeguards; no substantiated critical abuse found.
Core statements reconcile; immaterial disclosure errors are distinguished from material evidence gaps concerning deposits, government assets and interim cash.
Base requires about 68.38 crore peak year-end debt alongside new expansion and collateral; facilities and free deposits are not verified. Bear funding rises materially.
All 60 sessions observed and theoretical capacity is ample for the reference position, but a 29.28 percent lot and unverified live depth constrain execution.

limitations: No verified FY2027 interim balance-sheet bridge; annual forecasts begin from audited March balances and are conditional at the October entry date.
Exact unrestricted deposit amount and government-asset tax/GST composition are unresolved; reserve/recovery sensitivities prevent assuming them freely available.
New project engineering, customer qualification, debt sanctions and exact spend calendar are unverified; scenario capex/timing is not a financing commitment.
Historical customer concentration is known, but an equivalent current concentration table and independently re-opened rating rationale were not available.
ESOP grants and exercise terms remain unverified beyond authorized ceiling and floor; actual shares remain unchanged in the core model.
Live spreads/depth and all possible restrictions are not verified; IAS is conditional on a ₹5 lakh reference position and analytical assumptions.
